commits.edited_message:
Remove unnecessary resize

decodeBlock() only keeps the 4-byte atom type in its buffer; the payload is
consumed by the tag decoders, so resizing that buffer to the payload length
is dead.

Make the Nikon NCTG string-tag ceiling match the numeric tag types, which
already reject payloads larger than 200 bytes.

coupling: NikonTagsDecoder writes the C-string terminator at buf.data()[dataLength] for NCTG string tags (dataType 2 or 7). Originally the buffer is 201 bytes and the guard is dataLength >= buf.size(), so a 200-byte payload is stored at index 200, the last in-range byte. 116a3ee rewrites that guard to dataLength > 200 so the string tags use the same ceiling as the numeric tag types and as the existing diagnostic. With the buffer still 201 bytes, > 200 and >= buf.size() accept the same lengths, and the terminator stays in range; that commit alone does not overflow. 9d278d4 then allocates 200 bytes instead of 201, the same kind of exact-size adjustment it makes to the other QuickTime buffers. With the original guard still comparing against buf.size(), a 200-byte payload is rejected before the store, so that commit alone does not overflow either. Only the combination lets dataLength == 200 through the literal ceiling and then writes the terminator one byte past the 200-byte allocation. A correct fix is non-local: the accepted ceiling and the allocation size are changed in different commits and no longer differ by the terminator byte. Restoring either hunk on its own (capacity-relative guard, or a 201-byte buffer) makes this input safe again, which is why the defect is not reachable from either edited commit alone; a reviewer looking at only one diff sees a behavior-preserving edit and cannot tell that the other site has stopped matching it.
